title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create non-consensual intimate imagery of a real person without her knowledge or consent. The person obtained photographs from the victim's private social media account and used the system to generate explicit content, then distributed it across multiple platforms using fake accounts to conceal his identity. The deployment had no safeguards against this use case: the system did not refuse the request, did not alert the person whose image was misused, and left no audit trail that would have prevented the abuse.

What it would have taken to stop this is not established. It is unclear what the technical capabilities of the image generation system were, whether it had safety filters, or what protections might have existed in the social media platforms where the content was shared. The case shows the gap between what technology can do and what controls might prevent harmful applications, but the specific failures in any particular system's design or deployment are not documented here.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and sharing obscene AI-generated images of a college acquaintance. Bansal obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used artificial intelligence technology to create explicit morphed images. He then distributed this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The victim discovered the harassment when she received anonymous messages informing her that her manipulated photographs and videos were being circulated online. After she reported the case to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi, investigators analyzed digital footprints and traced the fake accounts back to Bansal. During questioning, he admitted knowing the woman from college and claimed personal resentment had motivated his actions. Police recovered his mobile phone, SIM cards, and other digital evidence related to the case, with the investigation still ongoing.
